root_cause: BR-OUTPUT Swift files violated L3 PURITY with non-ASCII characters; QueenStatusViewModel used /bin/zsh -c for health probes creating CWE-78 shell injection surface; singleton lock lived in world-writable /tmp; registry.json referenced a missing agent file.
fix_pattern: Batch-replace non-ASCII chars in BR-OUTPUT with ASCII equivalents per ascii-cleanup.md. Add run/runAsync tokenized Process helpers to QueenStatusViewModel and migrate all health probes. Move singleton lock/PID to .trinity/run/ with restricted perms. Remove agent-H from registry.json.
lessons: ASCII-only policy is enforceable with a single Python scan; batch replacement preserves semantics if done carefully.
Shell-free Process helpers dramatically reduce attack surface but require careful async actor crossing in @MainActor Swift.
Singleton lock path must be user-private; /tmp is unsafe for process identity.
Registry drift (missing agent-H) is a latent L1 TRACEABILITY bug; add CI validation.
